# ALGAL

> Programs that grow. More from every model. ALGAL is a language for typed,
> bounded agent programs, a foundation for a coding-agent harness, and a
> host-controlled environment for generating and selecting program populations.

Previously named Morphogen. The public package is @hraness/algal and the CLI is
algal. The existing morphogen.*.v1 wire identifiers and legacy fixtures are
preserved for digest and replay compatibility. New stores default to .algal;
--dir .morphogen reads an existing store without moving it.

## Source

- Repository: https://github.com/hraness/morphogen
- Design and implementation audit: docs/algal-design.md
- Language contract: spec/v1/organism.md
- Agent integration: docs/agent-tool.md and docs/executors.md
- Selection and populations: docs/civilization.md
- Measured case studies and limitations: docs/when-morphogen-wins.md

## Product boundaries

Manifests are data, not executable code. Host registries own functions, tools,
providers, and admission. Every run is bounded and emits a content-addressed
receipt. Replay checks deterministic orchestration with recorded external
answers; it does not establish that an answer is true, an external operation
really happened, or a provider was authenticated.

The two value propositions are a growing, inspectable agent harness and better
use of model capacity through evidence, structure, checks, and measurement.
The design has three layers: language/kernel, agent harness, and habitat.

## Migration status

The TypeScript v1 runtime is implemented and retained as the compatibility
reference. Native Rust execution, ACP integration, relational memory,
compaction, provider generalization, and an Apple Foundation Models bridge are
being developed against explicit tests. See docs/algal-design.md for current
qualification rather than assuming every proposed integration is production-ready.

AgentMixer is now xcb (https://github.com/hraness/xcb). Subscription credentials,
provider qualification, account custody, and settled quota-aware switching
belong to xcb, not to an ALGAL manifest. ACP is the client/agent protocol; it is
not an authentication or sandbox protocol.

Oh (https://oh.computer), Wordcell (https://github.com/hraness/wordcell), and
Gobstopper (https://github.com/hraness/gobstopper) inform native memory and
compaction: immutable sources, derived context, bounded positive logic, exact
recall, and no mutation of provider-owned transcripts by ALGAL.

## Run the compatibility reference

```sh
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run cli run examples/hello.algal.json
bun run cli suite
```

The billing-dispute example demonstrates the value of evidence access. An earlier
six-case run recorded Qwen plus a ledger lookup at 6/6 and an unassisted Opus
call at 4/6. This is not a controlled model comparison: the systems had different
tools. Historical prices are declared rate cards, not current billing promises.
The batch/ensemble experiments also found cases where decomposition added cost
without improving quality. Use the benchmark harness on your own workload.
